text: Bank of Baroda's savers are in India. Its fastest growing borrowers aren't.
Clue one. In India, deposits grew seventy five thousand crore more than loans.
Clue two. Abroad, loans grew fifty seven thousand crore more than deposits.
The twist. Overseas loans are a fifth of the book, but forty percent of the growth.
So, is it bad? Not by itself. The moat is at home. Indians hand Baroda more deposits than it lends here.
The open question is abroad. Who borrows, and what do they pay? Back to the napkin.
